name: frontend-engine-pin
body: For every frontend, the spec records the exact engine pin that sets its language-version ceiling, and says whether that ceiling is the pin alone or the user's toolchain. Pins: Go = `golang.org/x/tools v0.48.0` together with the compiling toolchain's `go/types` (ceiling = the installed Go toolchain); Java = the runtime JDK's `javac` via `ToolProvider.getSystemJavaCompiler()` (ceiling = the installed JDK ≥ 21); C++ = the vendored tree-sitter language ABI v15 plus the vendored tree-sitter-cpp grammar content itself (`src/cpplib/vendor/tree-sitter-cpp/src/parser.c` + `scanner.c`) — a content/ABI pin, because upstream ships no version for the vendored grammar; Rust = rust-analyzer tag `2026-08-17` (0.0.348) plus the user's `cargo`/`rustc` used to load the target project; TypeScript = `typescript 5.9.3`; C# = Roslyn `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp(.Workspaces) 4.12.0` parsed at `LanguageVersion.Latest`; Python = Ruff/ty tag `0.16.6` (salsa 0.27). The bundled structural scanner records its crates (serde/serde_json/unicode-normalization 0.1) but no language-version ceiling: the text/config formats have none to impose. Acceptance: all seven frontend containers record a pin or an explicit content/ABI identity, Go/Java/Rust state that their ceiling is the installed toolchain, and the bundled structural scanner records that it imposes no ceiling.
